To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) AS/HFA children have a ToM deficit, 2) the severity of autistic symptoms in children with AS/HFA is related to their ToM performance, 3) the severity of their autistic symptoms is related to the severity of autistic symptomatology of their parents, and 4) mothers of AS/HFAs have a ToM impairment, which is related to their child's severity of autistic symptoms.
AS/HFA children and their mothers had lower scores than their TD counterparts on the ToM Person index of the SAT task, and that AS/HFA mothers had lower scores on this index than fathers of AS/HFA.

the severity of ToM impairment in AS/HFA was positively correlated with the severity of autistic symptoms in children, and that mothers of AS/HFAs were less accurate than mothers of TD children on a ToM test, suggesting a possible role of mothers in the development of ToM impairment.

the ToM ability in children and their parents, the severity of autistic symptoms, and parental correlates.
the ability to attribute mental states to others (theory of mind) and autistic symptoms of children and parents of children diagnosed with AS.
the theory of mind ability of AS/HFA patients and their parents and with the severity of autistic symptoms.

the ToM deficit of AS/HFA is not a simple deficit but is a complex deficit.

AS/HFA children and their mothers are more deficient in ToM than TD children and their fathers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AS/HFA children have deficits in ToM ability, which are not necessarily related to the severity of the autism symptoms.
ToM deficits are present in AS/HFA and that the severity of autistic symptoms is correlated with ToM ability.
AS/HFA children are impaired in ToM and their mothers, but not their fathers, share this deficit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

AS/HFA children have a deficit in the ability to understand others' emotions, which is a core feature of ToM, and this deficit is associated with the severity of their autistic symptoms, particularly in social interaction.
the severity of autistic symptoms is related to the severity of the ToM deficit in both AS/HFA children and their mothers.

AS/HFA children and their parents are not only different from typically developing (TD), but also differ from each other on the ToM tasks, suggesting that the deficit is not only genetic, but also acquired through social interaction.
